Name: commit_then_consult_slot_discipline
Title: Anchoring, Not Overload: Commitment Order Explains Why Optimized Instructions and Agent Experience Memory Fight Each Other
Short Hypothesis: Harm from injected agent memory is a *slot violation resolved by order*: retrieved experience that is directive (imperative procedural content) occupies the demonstration slot but functions as an instruction, and because it arrives before the agent has committed to anything, it overrides plans the agent would otherwise have executed correctly. Three consequences, all testable at fixed injected-token count. (1) Ordering fix: commit-then-consult — draft and log a plan/answer with no memory, then revise against your own logged draft plus the *identical* retrieved items — sharply cuts breaks while preserving fixes, which the injection-volume account predicts it cannot. (2) Slot fix: routing the directive content out of the memory slot into the optimizer-owned instruction slot, where GEPA vets it against a training signal, neutralizes the same harm, and the two fixes are redundant rather than additive because they target one mechanism. (3) The risky coupling prediction: prompt optimization and memory are *anti-synergistic under memory-first ordering* — a GEPA-optimized instruction gives the agent a stronger correct prior to abandon, so memory harm gets **larger**, not smaller, after instruction optimization, and the anti-synergy disappears under commit-then-consult.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **Memory-harm mechanism papers.** MemHarness (2607.28272) attributes negative transfer to verbatim replay and fixes item *content*; "When Continual Learning Moves to Memory" (2604.27003) attributes it to experiences *competing for context* (the volume account); "Selective Memory Retention" (2606.29178) fixes the *write* path; ActMem (2603.00026) attributes it to similarity-based retrieval lacking causal structure; "Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory" (2603.02473) crosses write strategies with retrievers and finds retrieval quality dominates write strategy. Every one of these changes *what is in the context*. None changes *when the agent commits relative to seeing it*, and none reports a fix/break decomposition that separates "memory failed to help" from "memory overrode a correct plan."

(2) **The mirror-image finding.** "LLM Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers" (2601.22436) shows agents often *ignore* condensed experience, tracing this to semantic limits of condensation and internal biases that suppress experience. Its causal story runs opposite to ours (under-use vs. override). It is the strongest evidence that our effect is model- and item-dependent, which is why directiveness is a measured covariate here and not an assumption: their "suppression" regime and our "override" regime should separate along it.

(3) **Retrieval gating.** MemCon (2607.13591), AdaMEM (2606.05684), "To Retrieve or To Think?" (2601.08747), and meta-cognitive memory management (2601.07470) decide *whether/when/how much* to retrieve. We always retrieve everything and change only commitment order; gating cannot preserve fixes on instances it gates away.

(4) **Draft-then-verify and knowledge-conflict RAG.** Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) is structurally the closest ancestor of our A2: draft first, then verify. It verifies against the model's own generated questions, has no external experience memory, and is a factuality method, not an adjudication between competing accounts of agent-memory harm. Astute RAG / Madam-RAG (2504.13079) generate internal-knowledge passages alongside retrieved documents and reconcile in a single pass; Self-Refine and Speculative RAG draft *after* retrieval. We do not claim draft-then-revise is new machinery. We implement the closest such method as a numbered condition (A5) and the compute-matched no-memory version as another (A4). The claim is causal and comparative — that a *logged pre-retrieval commitment*, at token-matched injection, is what removes procedural override in an agent memory loop — plus the interaction with instruction optimization, which none of this literature touches.

(5) **Prompt optimization.** MIPRO and GEPA treat a prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over both; ExpeL/Reflexion/ReasoningBank/ExpRAG (2603.18272) fill the demonstration slot from accumulated experience. The composition is deployed but unexamined: no paper we found asks whether an *optimized* instruction makes memory more or less dangerous. Our anti-synergy prediction is the direct answer, and it is the opposite of what "the two components fail on disjoint slices, so combine them" would lead one to expect.
Abstract:
Agentic memory systems retrieve distilled past experience and place it in the agent's context before it acts. A 2026 wave of results shows this frequently hurts, and every proposed remedy edits the memory: prune it, reconstruct it, restructure retrieval, or retrieve less. We propose that a large share of the harm is neither content nor volume but **order**. Retrieved experience that reads as a directive ("always search the entity page first") is instruction-shaped content sitting in the demonstration slot; presented before the agent has committed to anything, it functions as a command rather than as evidence, and the agent abandons plans it would have executed correctly. A pilot is consistent with this: injecting a retrieved bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven — a one-sided signature noise does not produce.

We test the anchoring account with an intervention that changes only ordering: **commit-then-consult**, where the agent first produces and logs a plan/answer with no memory, then sees its own logged draft alongside the *identical* retrieved items. The deciding pass contains the same memory tokens as the standard agent, so the volume account predicts no benefit. We then push the account into the space the track cares about: if the harm is instruction-shaped content in the wrong slot, then (i) routing directives into the optimizer-owned instruction slot should fix it the same way, redundantly rather than additively, and (ii) **GEPA-optimized instructions should make memory-first injection more harmful, not less**, because a better instruction is a better prior to abandon. That anti-synergy, and its disappearance under commit-then-consult, is our sharpest and riskiest prediction. Fully paired McNemar designs, null replicates, a stated minimum detectable effect, a directly implemented single-pass reconciliation baseline, a content-rewriting baseline, and a smaller-k baseline that could each refute us.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED ACROSS ALL CONDITIONS:** ReAct scaffold, retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from a training split with an ExpeL-style write path, then frozen), decoding temperature and seed schedule, tool stack, step limit, prompt boilerplate. Only commitment ordering, memory variant, and instruction source differ.

**ENVIRONMENTS.** E1 (primary, carries all quantitative claims): tool-augmented multi-hop QA, HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue, agent issues search calls, 4–8 model calls/episode. E2 (replication only): ALFWorld, reduced grid, commitment is a subgoal sequence. **WebShop is dropped** — it added a third environment without a claim.

**MODELS.** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct primary (E1 + E2). Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the core E1 contrasts. **The 32B model is dropped**; the prediction is now "direction replicates on the second model," not "2 of 3." A frontier API model does offline write-path distillation, GEPA reflection, item annotation, and content rewriting — identically across conditions.

**BANK UTILITY PRECHECK (150-instance dev split).** Standard memory-first must flip ≥4% of instances wrong→right vs. no-memory; otherwise fix-preservation is untestable. We also inject the gold trajectory of the nearest training task on this dev split as an oracle ceiling on the bank's content value. Both numbers are reported, not used as gates in silence. Also on dev only: a position control (memory placed immediately before the action step rather than at context head) to rule out primacy artifacts.

**E1 CONDITION GRID (fully paired; every test instance under every condition).**
*Base-instruction ordering arm:*
- A0 No memory, single pass. Reference for all fix/break tables.
- A1 Memory-first, k=7. Standard deployment; the thing we claim is anchored.
- A2 **Commit-then-consult (ours).** Pass 1: no memory, produce answer + supporting trace, logged verbatim. Pass 2: task + own logged draft + identical k=7 items; keep or revise. Deciding-pass memory tokens identical to A1.
- A3 Draft-hidden second pass. Same two-pass structure, same memory, draft withheld. Isolates *having committed* from *getting a second pass*. Critical ablation.
- A4 Two-pass self-refine, no memory. Compute-matched, memory-free control.
- A5 **Single-pass reconciliation baseline (Astute-RAG / CoVe style; added at reviewer request).** One pass: state what you would do absent the retrieved experience, then reconcile against the k=7 items and answer. Same tokens, no logged commitment boundary. This is the cheap competitor that could beat us.
- A6 **Content-rewriting baseline (MemHarness style; added at reviewer request).** Retrieved items rewritten offline by the API model conditioned on the query, then injected memory-first. Run on a 300-instance subset for cost; reported with its own reduced MDE.
- A7 Volume fix: memory-first, k=3. The competing account's remedy and the strongest practical baseline.
- A8 Self-consistency control: A1 sampled twice with majority vote, matched to A2's call budget. Ensures the method is never credited for spending more compute.

*Coupling arm (the track's question).* One GEPA run on the train split optimizes the instruction with **no memory in the loop** (instruction-only, no demo search), producing I\*.
- G0 I\*, no memory. Isolates the optimizer's own contribution.
- G1 I\* + memory-first k=7. **The anti-synergy test.**
- G2 I\* + commit-then-consult.
- G3 **Directive routing.** An annotator extracts imperative/procedural content from bank items; a second, budget-capped GEPA run merges the surviving directives into the instruction slot; the memory slot retains episodic residue only; memory-first ordering. Tests whether the harm is *where the directive lives*.
- G4 G3 + commit-then-consult. Tests redundancy: if ordering and routing fix one mechanism, G4 ≈ G3 ≈ A2, not better than each.

**E2 (ALFWorld) grid:** A0, A1, A2, A3, A7 only, n=200, 2 seeds. Directional replication.
**Second model (Llama-3.1-8B) on E1:** A0, A1, A2, A3, G0, G1, G2, n=600, 1 seed.

**PRIMARY ANALYSIS.** For every condition, the paired fix/break table against its matched no-memory reference (A0 for the base arm, G0 for the coupling arm). Headline endpoints: (i) break count A2 vs. A1; (ii) fix count A2 vs. A1, non-inferiority at a pre-registered 2-point margin; (iii) the ordering × optimization interaction on break rate (A1−A0 vs. G1−G0). Net accuracy is secondary: a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention.

**MECHANISM READOUTS.** (a) Override rate: fraction of instances where the memory-conditioned first action differs from the no-memory first action, with accuracy conditional on divergence, for A1, A2, G1, G2. (b) Revision quality in A2/G2: helped/hurt ratio among instances the agent chose to revise. (c) Directiveness: LLM annotation of each item as imperative/directive vs. descriptive/episodic, validated against 150 human labels with Cohen's kappa; we test whether A1 break rate rises with top-1 item directiveness at controlled token count, and whether the directiveness→break slope *steepens* under I\* (the mechanism-level form of the anti-synergy claim).

**COMPUTE ARITHMETIC (hard envelope: 4×A100 80GB, days not weeks).**
E1: 13 full-n conditions × 600 = 7,800 episodes at seed 1; A6 subset 300; extra seeds — {A0,A1,A2,A3} at 3 seeds (+4,800) and {G0,G1,G2} at 2 seeds (+1,800). E1 total ≈ **14,700 episodes ≈ 125k model calls** (single-pass ≈6.5 calls/episode, two-pass ≈12). E2: 5 conditions × 200 × 2 seeds = 2,000 episodes ≈ 40k calls (longer horizons). Second model: 7 × 600 = 4,200 episodes ≈ 31k calls (8B, faster). GEPA: 2 runs × ~800 rollouts = 1,600 episodes. **Total ≈ 22,500 episodes / ~200k model calls.** At pilot-measured vLLM throughput on this node (~1.5–3k calls/hour for a 14B with tensor-parallel 2 and two replicas), this is **≈2.5–3 days of node time**, leaving headroom for reruns. API spend: ~1,000 distillation calls, ~1,350 annotation calls (1,200 items + 150 validated), ~2,100 content rewrites, ~200 long-context GEPA reflection calls ≈ **$150–250**, inside the stated budget. Cut relative to the previous version: WebShop, the 32B model, an asymmetric-revision-bar condition, a k=3 commit-then-consult condition, an oracle test condition (demoted to dev precheck), and one seed on the coupling arm.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.**
- A7 (k=3, memory-first): pilot evidence says retrieving less already eliminates harm. If A7 matches A2 on *both* breaks and fixes, the volume account wins and we report it.
- A5 (single-pass reconciliation, Astute-RAG/CoVe style): the reviewer-named closest existing technique, now an actual run condition. If A5 matches A2, the logged commitment boundary is doing nothing and the contribution reduces to "prompt it to consider its own view first" — a real result, reported as such.
- A6 (MemHarness-style situation-conditioned rewriting): if content rewriting beats ordering, the content account wins.
- A4 (two-pass self-refine, no memory): if it matches A2, the effect is deliberation, not ordering, and the paper collapses.
- A8 (self-consistency at matched calls): guards against crediting extra compute.
- G0 (GEPA instructions, no memory): if G0 dominates everything with memory, the practical recommendation for the track is "optimize instructions and drop the bank," which is itself a decisive answer to the division-of-labour question.

**ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.**
- A3 (draft hidden) is the critical one: two-pass structure and memory tokens fixed, only the logged commitment removed. Any A2−A3 gap is attributable to the anchor.
- G3 vs. A1: same directive content, different slot, same ordering. Isolates slot from order.
- G4 vs. G3 and A2: tests the redundancy prediction that follows from a single mechanism. If G4 is meaningfully better than both, we have two mechanisms, not one, and say so.
- G1−G0 vs. A1−A0: the interaction, i.e. whether optimization amplifies anchoring.
- Directiveness regression and override-rate readouts: non-accuracy evidence that the failure is override rather than load.

**COST ACCOUNTING.** Every condition reported on three matched axes: agent calls, wall clock, total tokens. A2 roughly doubles E1 calls; A8 and A4 exist so the comparison is never compute-flattering.
Falsifiable Predictions:
If the anchoring/slot account is right:
1. **P1 (ordering).** A2's break count on E1 is at most half A1's (e.g. ~10% of instances → <5%), exact McNemar p<0.05, same direction across 3 seeds and on Llama-3.1-8B.
2. **P2 (fixes preserved).** A2's fix count is non-inferior to A1's within a 2-point margin. A loss of 2–3 points is pre-registered as *inconclusive*, not as success.
3. **P3 (the anchor, not the second pass).** A3 recovers less than half of A2's break reduction.
4. **P4 (anti-synergy — the risky coupling claim).** Memory-first harm is *larger* under optimized instructions: break rate of G1 (vs. G0) exceeds break rate of A1 (vs. A0) by a factor ≥1.5 and ≥3 absolute points, with a bootstrap CI on the difference-in-differences excluding zero; and G2 (vs. G0) restores the break rate to at or below A2's. Correspondingly, the directiveness→break slope is steeper under I\* than under the base instruction.
5. **P5 (redundancy).** G3's break rate is within 2 points of A2's, and G4 improves on neither by more than 2 points — one mechanism, two entry points.
6. **P6 (override signature).** A1's override rate exceeds 25% with conditional accuracy on overridden instances below unconditional no-memory accuracy; A2 cuts the override rate by ≥1/3 and raises conditional accuracy.

**REFUTATION.** If A2's break count is statistically indistinguishable from A1's at identical memory tokens, the anchoring account is dead and the volume/content accounts stand — reported as a clean negative that strengthens the competing literature. If A2 cuts breaks but loses >3 points of fixes, the method merely teaches the agent to ignore memory, which is no better than not retrieving. If A5 matches A2, the commitment boundary is inert and the finding is a prompt-level one. If A7 matches A2 everywhere, the recommendation reduces to "retrieve less." If P4 inverts — optimized instructions *reduce* memory harm — the division of labour is benign, GEPA and memory are complementary as the field assumes, and our slot-violation framing is wrong; that is a publishable correction to our own thesis and we will report it as one.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Fully paired: every test instance runs under every condition with the same seed schedule; all comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar on paired outcome tables (A2 vs. A1 for breaks; A2 vs. A1 for fixes as non-inferiority at a 2-point margin), Holm-corrected across the condition family, with the full fix/break decomposition printed beside every delta. The interaction (P4) is a difference-in-differences of paired break proportions on the same instances, with CIs from a 10k-resample instance-level bootstrap, and confirmed by a mixed-effects logistic model with instance random intercept and terms for memory, optimization, and their product.

**NOISE FLOOR.** For each environment and model, identical conditions re-run under different decoding seeds serve as null replicates; we report the distribution of apparent deltas and claim no effect that does not exceed its 95th percentile. This is load-bearing, not decorative: prior pilot work in this setting saw 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets, and a treatment-free null replicate produced the same apparent gain as the best real treatment.

**MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECT, stated per claim.**
- P1 (break endpoint, one-sided, n=600): with A1 breaks near 60/600 and a predicted halving, ~30 one-sided discordant events give power >0.9 at α=0.05. This is the best-powered arm and it carries the main claim.
- Net accuracy (secondary): with an expected 12–18% discordance rate, McNemar detects ≈4 points at 80% power. We do not claim net-accuracy effects below that.
- P2 (fix non-inferiority): detectable only to ≈3 points at this n. Pre-registered: a 2–3 point fix loss is reported as inconclusive.
- P4 (interaction): the weakest arm. With 600 instances × 3 seeds (base) / 2 seeds (coupling) pooled in the mixed model, the difference-in-differences is powered to detect roughly a doubling of break rate (e.g. 6%→12% or 10%→20%), not a 2-point shift. We therefore state P4 as a *ratio* prediction (≥1.5× and ≥3 absolute points) rather than a fine-grained one, and a CI overlapping zero is reported as inconclusive on the coupling with the ordering claim standing independently.
- E2 (n=200, MDE ≈7 points) and the second model are directional replication only; no primary claim rests on them alone.
- Directiveness annotation validated on 150 human-labelled items with Cohen's kappa; treated as supporting evidence.
Preprint Collision Check:
Grounded in the search just run plus three earlier rounds. Named closest recent work and verdicts:

- **"LLM Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers" (2601.22436) — closest, does not collide, and constrains us.** It is a controlled-intervention study of when agents fail to integrate condensed experience, but its finding is that agents *ignore or suppress* experience, attributing this to semantic limits of condensation and internal biases plus regimes where priors suffice. That is the mirror image of override. It does not manipulate commitment order, does not decompose fixes vs. breaks, and does not touch instruction optimization. Its existence is a genuine risk to P6 (there may be model/item regimes where suppression dominates override), which is exactly why directiveness is a measured covariate and why per-model curves are reported rather than pooled.
- **ActMem (2603.00026) — competing account, no collision.** Attributes negative transfer to surface-similarity retrieval and fixes it with event-centric causal memory structure; changes what is retrieved, never when the agent commits.
- **"Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory" (2603.02473, v2 Apr 2026) — closest methodologically, no collision, and partly supportive.** It crosses write strategies with retrievers and finds retrieval quality dominates write strategy. That is consistent with our pilot finding that write-path repairs neutralized but did not convert the harm; it locates the problem on the read side but never varies commitment order, and its utilization axis is retrieval quality, not slot or sequence.
- **ExpRAG (2603.18272)** is the standard inject-then-decide architecture we take as A1. **MemEvoBench (2604.15774)** is safety/poisoning-focused. **"Learning How to Remember" (ACL Findings 2026, 2601.07470)** and the **CBR-for-LLM-agents review (2504.06943)** are management/framing work. None tests ordering.
- From earlier rounds: **MemHarness (2607.28272)** (content rewriting — now implemented as A6), **"When Continual Learning Moves to Memory" (2604.27003)** (the volume account our token-matched contrast is built to adjudicate against), **MemCon (2607.13591) / AdaMEM (2606.05684) / "To Retrieve or To Think?" (2601.08747)** (gating whether/when, not order), **Astute RAG / Madam-RAG (2504.13079)** (single-pass reconciliation — now implemented as A5), **Speculative RAG / Self-Refine** (drafting after retrieval — A4).
- **Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) — flagged by a reviewer, added here, and conceded as the closest structural ancestor.** CoVe drafts then verifies, so we do not claim draft-then-revise as new machinery. CoVe verifies against self-generated questions with no external experience store, targets factuality, and never compares token-matched orderings or adjudicates competing accounts of agent-memory harm. We now run its nearest agent-memory analogue (A5) as a numbered condition rather than distinguishing it in prose.

**Honest gap.** The search budget was again exhausted before an OpenReview/ICLR-2026 and ACL/EMNLP-2025-26 proceedings sweep for "plan-before-memory" or "ordering ablation" appendices. I assume a nontrivial probability that a draft-then-consult ordering appears as an appendix ablation somewhere. Nothing retrieved in either round isolates ordering/commitment timing as the causal lever, and nothing at all reports the ordering × instruction-optimization interaction (P4), which is now the paper's sharpest claim and, on current evidence, unclaimed.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Zero-fix bank.** If the bank produces essentially no fixes, as in the pilot, the fix-preservation half of the claim is untestable. The dev-split utility precheck and oracle ceiling detect this; we report both rather than proceeding quietly.
2. **A5 may suffice.** The single-pass reconciliation baseline is now in the grid precisely because it might match A2. If it does, our contribution shrinks to a prompt-level finding plus the coupling result. We took that risk deliberately rather than leaving the competitor in prose.
3. **Compute asymmetry.** A2 roughly doubles E1 calls. A4 and A8 control for it, but the honest framing is "ordering is a cheaper fix than curation, not a free one."
4. **P4 is the least-powered arm.** The interaction is powered to detect a doubling of break rate, not a small shift, and rests on a single GEPA run per arm — the optimized instruction I\* is one draw, so a null could be an artifact of that draw. We report I\*'s own gain (G0 vs. A0) and the per-seed break rates so the reader can judge; we do not claim a null interaction as evidence of no coupling.
5. **Suppression regimes.** Per 2601.22436, some models under-use rather than over-follow experience. In such a regime A1 breaks will be low and P1 becomes untestable, not false. The precheck exposes this before the grid runs, and strong model dependence is reported as a finding, not averaged away.
6. **Coarse commitment in ALFWorld.** A pass-1 plan may be too vague to anchor. We require a concrete subgoal sequence and report E2 separately rather than pooling.
7. **Order and volume are not fully separable internally.** Token-matching controls the input, not the model's internal attention allocation, so a strong A2 result is evidence for ordering rather than proof; the override-rate and directiveness readouts triangulate.
8. **Prompt-surface tuning.** The pass-2 and routing prompts are fixed in advance on a 100-instance dev split and reported verbatim; A5 checks whether a much simpler single-pass variant suffices.
9. **Negative-result exposure.** If ordering does nothing, the contribution rests on the measurement protocol and on the coupling result — which is why null replicates and per-claim MDEs are load-bearing.
